wording: - **In scope.** A person with a residence or habitual abode in Germany is fully liable to income tax on worldwide income (§ 1(1) EStG). This skill covers such a person whose income is mainly employment income (§ 19 EStG), with or without a spouse, with or without children.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Married couples and registered partners.** They may choose joint assessment (Zusammenveranlagung) if both are fully liable, not permanently separated, and met both conditions at some point in the year (§ 26(1) EStG). If neither chooses, joint assessment applies (§ 26(3) EStG).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Out of scope.** Non-residents with German wages (limited liability, § 1(4) EStG, or the § 1(3) election): use de-non-resident-tax. Self-employed, trade, capital and rental income go to the sibling skills listed above, then the results come back into this return.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

The allowances are always used for the solidarity surcharge and church tax base (§ 3(2) SolzG, § 51a(2) EStG).

wording: | Payment | An extra payment is due one month after the notice (§ 36(4) EStG). The tax office may also set quarterly prepayments for later years |
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Late-filing surcharge (§ 152 AO).** Only for mandatory filers. The tax office may set it after a late return. It must set it if the return is not in within 14 months after year end (for 2026: by 29 February 2028) unless an extension was granted, the tax is nil, or the tax does not exceed the wage tax withheld and prepayments (§ 152(2) and (3) AO). Amount: 0.25% per month or part month of the tax less withheld tax and prepayments, at least EUR 25 per month, at most EUR 25,000 (§ 152(5) and (10) AO). An employee due a refund is not hit by the mandatory surcharge.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Interest on the balance (§ 233a AO).** Runs from 15 months after year end, so from 1 April 2028 for 2026, until the notice takes effect. 0.15% per full month, 1.8% a year (§ 238(1a) AO), on the balance rounded down to EUR 50. Refunds earn the same interest, at the earliest from the day the tax was paid.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Late payment (§ 240 AO).** 1% per started month on the overdue amount rounded down to EUR 50.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Foreign pay of a resident.** Pay exempt in Germany under a tax treaty is still declared (Anlage N-AUS) and raises the rate on the rest (§ 32b EStG). Foreign tax credits under § 34c EStG are not covered here.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Moving in or out in 2026.** Months of limited liability and German-exempt foreign income are handled under § 2(7) and § 32b EStG; the pack has no method yet. For shares and departure rules see leaving-germany-exit-tax.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

wording: - **Spouse living abroad.** An EU/EEA national may get joint assessment with a spouse resident in the EU/EEA under § 1a EStG; filing is then mandatory (§ 46(2) no. 7 EStG). Not covered further.
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending

section: Example 1: single employee, EUR 55,000, commuter with home office days
wording: Lena is 30, single, no children, not a church member, works in Hesse, statutory health insurance with a fund additional rate of 2.9%. Gross 2026 pay EUR 55,000, all under the health ceiling of EUR 69,750. She went to the office on 120 days (30 km one way) and worked from home on 100 days. Work equipment EUR 250. Her wage tax certificate shows Lohnsteuer withheld of EUR 8,060 and no solidarity surcharge. (Invented case; EUR 8,060 is what the 2026 payroll formula in de-payroll gives for class I with these facts.)

section: Example 2: married couple, classes III and V, one child, splitting
wording: Jonas earns EUR 72,000 (class III, 15 km on 200 days, so commuting is EUR 1,140 and the EUR 1,230 lump sum is higher). Mia earns EUR 18,000 (class V) and pays EUR 200 union dues; she has no other job costs. One child, Kindergeld EUR 3,108 for the year. Both in statutory health insurance at a 2.9% additional rate, both work outside Saxony (so care is 1.8% each), no church. Because one spouse was in class V, they must file (§ 46(2) no. 3a EStG). Wage tax withheld on both certificates together: EUR 9,414 (invented case; worked out with the § 39b(2) EStG formula for these facts: class III EUR 7,564, class V EUR 1,850 at the 14% minimum; a payroll run can differ by a few euros).
status: inventory only; source binding/read classification pending
